items.title: Standalone AI Call Analysis API
items.impact: A new public API lets clients start call analysis from a secure recording link, retrieve result details and receive webhook updates.
items.role: I shaped the request contract with product, frontend and AI teams, implemented the backend across six repositories, and carried the work through QA and production.
items.timeline: Released to QA and production · August 2026 · {{prs_ai_api}} merged PRs across {{repositories_ai_api}} repositories

decisions.label: Accept links, not uploads
decisions.detail: File upload and an asynchronous worker were explicitly left out of scope; the API starts analysis from a secure HTTPS recording URL.

decisions.label: Bound the work
decisions.detail: Only HTTPS links were accepted, and analysis was limited to recordings up to two hours. Duration parsing was corrected for MP4, AMR and OGG recordings.

decisions.label: Keep the result path explicit
decisions.detail: The contract included endpoints to start analysis, check status and fetch details, with a webhook for results.

challenge: The product needed a standalone way for clients outside the dialer workflow to submit call recordings for analysis.
The request and result flow had to work with secure recording links, respect duration limits, and fit existing account and credit rules.
approach: Defined the request shape with product, frontend and AI stakeholders, then delivered the work across {{repositories_ai_api}} repositories in {{prs_ai_api}} merged pull requests.
Accepted HTTPS recording links, enforced a two-hour duration cap, and fixed duration detection for MP4, AMR and OGG.
Implemented the start, status and details endpoints alongside webhook delivery and existing credit handling.
Kept file upload and an asynchronous worker out of the initial scope.
impact_points: Released to QA and production in August 2026.
Three production-sensitive issues were addressed in follow-up work.
Usage and adoption figures were not recorded in the supplied work history; no business-impact metric is claimed.
lessons: Release was not the end of the work: three production-sensitive issues needed follow-up. I treat release verification and operational fixes as part of delivering a feature.
The source record has no API usage or adoption data, so I am not using call-volume or business-impact estimates for this project.

items.title: Lead Intelligence
items.impact: Lead Intelligence stores AI-generated lead summaries, health scores and conversion predictions so teams can prioritize follow-up.
items.role: I delivered the backend across eight repositories and raised scope changes with the product manager, including removing dialer integration and reverting the usage-charging change.
items.timeline: Released in v8.2 · {{prs_lead_intelligence}} merged PRs across {{repositories_lead_intelligence}} repositories

decisions.label: Keep scope explicit
decisions.detail: Dialer integration was removed from the story mid-delivery. A usage-charging change was built, tested and then reverted.

decisions.label: Handle missing AI data
decisions.detail: The AI-service webhook integration included edge cases for missing data; reporting used the latest lead record per customer.

challenge: Sales teams wanted lead scores derived from call analysis so they could prioritize likely buyers.
The feature touched persistent lead data, AI-service webhooks, customer and allocation filters, permissions, reports and call-log columns.
approach: Created a scoring formula for the demo, then implemented lead records and the API that returns them.
Connected the AI-service webhook, handling cases where data was missing.
Added filters, permissions, report columns and call-log columns across the agreed product surfaces.
impact_points: Released in v8.2 after {{prs_lead_intelligence}} merged PRs across {{repositories_lead_intelligence}} repositories.
Release testing identified several issues that were traced; later follow-up work is recorded separately.
Adoption and business-impact figures are not recorded in the supplied work history.

items.title: Data management permission restructuring
items.impact: Data-management permissions were split and restructured across admin web and user-update flows.
items.role: I executed the revised story and re-read its requirements after the user story changed.
challenge: The data-management permission model needed to be split and restructured.
approach: Separated the admin-web permission from the admin permission and updated process and user changes.
Addressed null handling in the web-allocation flow.
impact_points: Merged in March–April 2026 after {{prs_permissions}} merged PRs.
